question:
Let \(f(x,y)=xy\), where \(x\ge0\) and \(y\ge0\). Prove that the function \(f\) satisfies the following property:
\[
f(\lambda x+(1-\lambda)x',\lambda y+(1-\lambda)y')>\min\{f(x,y),f(x',y')\}
\]
for all \((x,y)\ne(x',y')\) and for all \(\lambda\in(0,1)\).

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
